status: Seven-code community-perspectives inquiry design through four existing shared operations. No new community, inquiry, map or identity claim.

wholeClaimChecks: FW9: three actual learner-formulated research questions, at least two sources for each, brief organised print notes and a written two-source synthesis.
Author points/reasons/evidence: identify actual claims and evaluate relevant/sufficient support rather than infer purpose makes a source automatically true or false.
Evidence-based writing: original accurate cited/paraphrased analysis and two-source synthesis, noting agreement and differences.

Familiar-map reading AND drawing: own classroom/school/park map, key/labels/relative landmarks/route remain a separate full-claim check. Historical/current Canada overlays are an additional application, not a replacement.
claimReview.readiness: Same complete Shared Research, Author Purpose, Main Topic/Paragraph Details and familiar-plan hard supports reviewed for the B2 programme remain unchanged and unassumed. No source-specific floor lowering or forced prerequisite associations.
claimReview.excluded: Historical facts remain the existing particular repertoires. Neither an Australian migration inventory nor scientific data/graphing inventory is added merely to make a chart. Genuine differing accounts do not mean all contradictory factual claims are equally supported.

networks-and-community.question: How did particular Indigenous–French trading relationships and later Métis community networks affect community experiences, and how do the selected accounts frame them?
sources: Museum of History Fur Trade, selected earlier exchanges and Métissages sections
MNO actual timeline and 2014 Mattawa/Nipissing study summary
networks-and-community.perspectiveCheck: Distinguish museum synthesis drawing on colonial records from an attributed Métis community account of collective emergence. Compare an actual shared claim about kinship/trade and each source’s focus; do not call two MNO pages independent corroboration or turn ancestry alone into identity.

community-responses.question: How did different settler communities describe or respond to barriers and community needs, and what do primary and later accounts allow us to conclude?
requiredCases: New France 1667 religious/community record as a dated contrast
sources: Parks Buxton account and Presbyterian Archives mission account
OJA Toronto hospital account and CMHR historical context
Actual 1667 marriage record/transcript and museum contextual explanation
community-responses.perspectiveCheck: Separate mission, historical commemoration and community institutional accounts. The authentic 1667 record establishes a particular rite/record, not every resident’s belief/access. Keep the actual 1832–35 Traill letter available as an attributed first-person contrast, not a neutral census. Do not invent an authentic voice or backdate a later school.

continuing-cultural-agency.question: How do particular First Nation, Métis and Inuit community accounts describe language/knowledge-sharing contributions and continuing identities, and what do those accounts leave unknown?
sources: Actual MNO Métis languages initiatives page
Actual Pirurvik Aurniarvik page, with the separately attributed Leena Evic account if used
continuing-cultural-agency.perspectiveCheck: Actually use the three distinct community sources. Compare their purposes, audience, stated programmes and identity relationships; institutional descriptions are not interviews with every learner or measured efficacy. Adult Inuit English-first-language classes do not establish pupil Inuktut proficiency. A present account does not prove every colonial cause or universal community agreement.

preparedMapTasks.base: Use the verified locator resources and actual 1811 Cary map with its author/date, plus a current Canada political reference. The northern location text/globe reference is a locator aid, not a claimed historical map.
analysis: Analyse the actual historical map in a legible print excerpt and a digital view. Identify broad Great Lakes/St. Lawrence orientation, the colonial publisher’s selection/omissions and the inability of this map to establish complete Indigenous presence/consent or current title.

Compare it with a current Canada reference and source-attributed case locations. Later Mattawa, Buxton and Toronto facts must be explicitly dated annotations, not facts supposedly printed on an 1811 map.
construction: Construct a print annotated historical/community map using actual supported case labels, date and key. Use broad placements supported by the locator packets; do not invent exact boundaries, sites or travel routes.

Construct a digital thematic map of the actually selected historical/current community cases and source perspectives, with a key distinguishing actual event/place dates from source publication dates. The task must explain how its spatial pattern helps answer a question; no arbitrary source-mention counts or ethnicity-density inference.

For a current cultural-source case outside the detailed southern base, use the current verified locator/globe and actual community location resource. Do not squeeze a northern case into an Upper/Lower Canada map.

preparation: Adult setup: provide substantial legible selected print and digital material from the actual source packets, retaining creator/publisher/date/place, and a question/source/fact/perspective/limit note organiser. Original summaries support access but do not mislabel themselves primary sources.

Provide at least one actual primary document, such as the 1667 record/transcript or the selected Traill letter, and actual secondary historical/community accounts. Supply the actual historical/current map references with legible excerpts. Exclude unviewed images, source slurs and unsafe unrelated site content.
actions: Formulate three actual inquiry questions with different perspectives on several distinct Canadian communities, using the models as supports. Gather at least two suitable sources for EACH question; the programme actually uses distinct First Nation, Métis, Inuit and more than one settler community case, not merely lists their availability.

Take brief print-source notes under meaningful headings and gather further digital evidence. Record who created each account, when, what type of evidence it is and whose experience/interest is represented or absent. Separate a primary record, original memoir/letter, historical synthesis and present institutional account.

Complete both analysis AND construction in print AND digital mapping as specified by preparedMapTasks. Carry the selected question and actual dated case through notes, source comparison, map annotations and conclusions. Retain the complete familiar-place map check separately.

Use an actual perspective comparison matrix: claim, evidence, source role/purpose, support/agreement/difference and unresolved question. For example, compare Parks’ settlement/heritage focus with the mission archive’s 1849–50 schooling account, or the museum’s earlier kinship explanation with MNO’s later collective-community account. Shared underlying records limit independence; matching dates are not proof of every claim.

Evaluate the evidence rather than impersonate participants: explain a supported community experience, an actual difference in perspective/focus and a conclusion the packet cannot justify. Do not infer a person’s feelings from ancestry, a group label, a bare photograph or an institution’s promotional purpose.

Write an original cited two-source synthesis noting agreement and difference, and present an oral explanation with actual print/digital map products and the evidence organiser. Use relevant vocabulary accurately, such as source, perspective, settler/newcomer, community, continuity/change, identity and exclusion, without importing a whole unrelated terminology inventory.
successEvidence: Three actual questions; at least two suitable sources for each; organised print notes and actual primary AND secondary evidence.
Several distinct communities and genuine supported perspectives, including actual use of the three Indigenous community cases in this designed programme.
Print AND digital map analysis AND construction with attribution/date/key and meaningful inquiry role.
Original evidence evaluation/conclusions and cited two-source communication with agreement/difference and stated source limits.
nearMisses: Adult supplies answers under three headings but the learner never formulates questions or uses a second source for each.
Invents dialogue, supposes an institutional account is every community member’s view, or relabels a modern summary as a primary diary.
Only looks at a map or annotates later facts without dates; forces an irrelevant chart to tick an inventory.
Copies source text or says two accounts agreeing proves all their claims or all present outcomes.

whole-inquiry.operation: Complete the coherent inquiryProtocol and actual case/perspective/map requirements; this is not a mechanical overall rollup.

questions.operation: Formulate and pursue three actual questions covering the supported models, several distinct communities and differing perspectives; two sources per question.

gathering.operation: Actually gather and organise both primary and secondary print/digital evidence with creator/date/place/source-type and different perspectives.

maps.operation: Complete actual print AND digital analysis AND construction in preparedMapTasks, preserving source dates, map omissions and actual familiar-map whole-claim requirements.

analysis.operation: Interpret actual evidence using question-led perspective/source comparison and meaningful dated/map organisers; no arbitrary counting or invented participant feelings.

conclusions.operation: Evaluate actual support and source purposes/limits; draw original conclusions about distinct community experiences and differing perspectives, not stereotypes or an assumption all opinions are equally factual.

communication.operation: Original cited/paraphrased report and oral/map presentation, using relevant terms and actual source agreement/difference with cultural attribution.

coverageBoundary: Source-fit authoring programme, not classroom observations, every historical fact/source endorsement or overall A1/A3 completion. Existing particular knowledge claims and actual learner readiness remain distinct.
